key_idea: Capacities only increase, so the previous flow stays feasible: after each improvement just bump the residual capacities and continue augmenting from the current flow instead of recomputing max flow from scratch.
sketch: Store the undirected network as an n x n residual capacity matrix (cap[a][b] += c and cap[b][a] += c). Run Dinic once for the initial answer; for each improvement add c to both directions of the residual matrix and run Dinic again on the existing residual graph, adding the newly found flow to the running total. Each update costs at least one BFS, O(n^2) = 1e4, so 1e4 updates are about 1e8 trivial operations, plus augmentation work bounded by the total flow growth. Pitfalls: pipes are bidirectional, the source is station 1 and the sink station 2, improvements may create new pipes or repeat pairs, and a from-scratch max flow per query would be too slow.
